objectives: Hear /f/ followed by /l/ at the start of a taught word.
Blend initial /fl/ smoothly without inserting an extra vowel.
Identify words beginning with fl and distinguish them from words beginning with f alone.
Use sound evidence to identify the whole word.
concepts: A consonant blend contains adjacent consonant phonemes that remain audible.
The fl onset contains /f/ followed by /l/.
Smooth blending keeps the consonants close without inserting a vowel.
Listening for /l/ distinguishes fl-words from words beginning with /f/ alone.

definitions.definition: Two adjacent consonant sounds that can both be heard, such as /f/ and /l/ in flag.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.
Joining phonemes closely in order without inserting an extra vowel.

workedExamples.prompt: Say the first two sounds in flap.

workedExamples.solution: Keep /f/ and /l/ close and blend to read flip.
Flag has /f/ then /l/; fag has /f/ without /l/.

commonMistakes: Skipping /l/ and reading flag as fag.
Guessing from f without checking the next sound.
keyTakeaways: Keep both consonants audible and close together.
Flap, flip, flop, flag and flat begin with fl.
Check the whole word after blending.
revisionPoints: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
Contrast flap with fan to hear the difference.

basic.prompt: Name a word that begins with fl.
Which word begins with fl: flip or fan?

conceptual.prompt: Why is fl a consonant blend?
conceptual.answer: Both /f/ and /l/ can be heard in order.

conceptual.prompt: What should you avoid between /f/ and /l/?
How is flag different from fag?
conceptual.answer: Flag has /l/ after /f/; fag does not.

application.prompt: Which word begins with fl and has short /i/?

application.answer: Blend /f/ and /l/ closely to say flop.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why listen for /l/ when identifying an fl-word?
higherOrderThinking.answer: It distinguishes fl from words beginning with /f/ alone.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can you check a guessed word?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Say each phoneme in order and blend the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Which contrast helps hear fl: flag/fan or flag/flat?
higherOrderThinking.answer: flag/fan, because it contrasts fl with /f/ alone.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in flat?
Which word begins with fl and ends in /p/?

mixedReview.answer: An extra vowel between the consonants

activities.name: Hear and blend fl-words.
steps: Say both sounds close together without an extra vowel.
Blend the vowel and final sounds.
Repeat with flap, flip, flop, flag and flat.

activities.name: Contrast fl-words with words beginning with f alone.
steps: Sort flap, flag, flat, fan and fit.
Say the first two sounds in each word.
Read each word to confirm the sort.
